title: stream-lease-heartbeat-fallback-toolcall-confirmation-openai-compat
author: Nina Park
release_notes: Add server-side lease watchdog + client heartbeat with fallback routing; introduce tool-call confirmation token to ensure idempotent function/tool calls across reconnects. Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI streaming events; small client-side SDK update required for optimal behavior.
description:
Motivation: Improve stream lifecycle robustness in client disconnect/reconnect scenarios while preserving OpenAI-compatible semantics. We observed increased user-facing duplicate tool invocations and opaque stream terminations when a client rejoined after a network hiccup. This PR introduces a lightweight server lease/watchdog and a client heartbeat protocol plus small changes to the OpenAI compatibility adapter to handle soft cancels and resume semantics with explicit tool-call confirmation tokens.

What this PR does (single string): Adds a lease-based server watchdog that keeps a short-lived lease for active streaming sessions and enforces a soft-quarantine on abandoned sessions. Implements a client heartbeat (periodic ping tied to the session lease) so the server can distinguish short disconnects from abandoned streams. Introduces a confirmation token attached to tool/function call events: when the server emits a tool call to a downstream executor, it attaches a monotonically-increasing confirmation id; on reconnect the client and server reconcile outstanding confirmation ids to avoid duplicate retries. The OpenAI adapter maps the new internal soft-cancel event to the existing stop/abort codes and maintains the previous wire format for backwards compatibility. Adds configuration knobs: lease_ttl, heartbeat_interval, reconnect_grace_window, and fallback_routing_policy (how to route resumed sessions to alternate capacity pools). Includes unit and integration tests that simulate flaky connectivity, delayed reconnects, and tool call retries.

Commit summary: (high level)
- a1b3d2c: add lease manager and watchdog loop, TTL enforcement and metrics
- 7f4e1b0: implement client heartbeat handler and reconciler logic on reconnect
- 3c9b8a7: tool-call confirmation token plumbing through runtime and adapter layer
- ef5d2a1: openai_compat: map soft-cancel + resume semantics to existing streaming events
- d1a7cbb: tests: stream resume, orphaned lease reconciliation, toolcall idempotency harness
- c8b4f99: docs and examples: openai compat upgrade notes + migration guide

Files changed (high level):
- src/streaming/lease_manager.py (new): lease lifecycle, metrics, and TTL enforcement
- src/streaming/watchdog.py (new): background watchdog to detect orphaned sessions and trigger fallback
- src/streaming/heartbeat.py (modified): heartbeat handler + reconcilier
- src/openai_compat/stream_adapter.py (modified): map soft-cancel/resume and carry confirmation token in stream events
- tests/stream/test_resume_and_toolcall.py (new): deterministic harness for reconnect/toolcall idempotency
- examples/openai-streaming-migration.md (new): migration notes for SDKs
- docs/operational/lease_and_heartbeat.md (new): runbook and tuning guidance
- examples/benchmarks/lease-overhead.md (modified): small perf numbers and CI benchmark updates

Runtime behavior and compatibility notes: The server-side lease default TTL is conservative (20s) with a heartbeat_interval of 5s. Short disconnects less than reconnect_grace_window (config default 30s) are fast-reconciled and the runtime attempts to reuse the same backing execution slot. If the lease expires the watchdog marks the session quarantined and triggers fallback routing: either resume on warm standby or redirect to another region/pool depending on policy. Tool-call confirmation ids are opaque strings but deterministic per-session; clients that do not opt into the new confirmation flow continue to receive the same streaming payloads but may observe duplicate tool invocations in pathological reconnect cases. The OpenAI wire format remains compatible: we reuse the streaming "stop" and "done" events and add an optional "x-confirmation-id" field on tool-call structured events (adapter strips unknown fields for older clients).

Testing and CI: Initial runs surfaced a flaky race in the test harness where the watchdog TTL and artificial network pauses needed tighter coordination; addressed by adding deterministic clock mocking in tests. CI matrix: unit (pytest) / integration (docker-compose streaming harness) / lint (flake8) / type checks. First pipeline run: unit tests failed (reconciler race); fix pushed in commit 3c9b8a7 and CI re-run passed.

Review conversation highlights:
- Arjun Mehta (reviewer): "Please surface a metric for lease_reclaimed_count and ensure we emit a debug log with session id and reason when fallback routing triggers."
- Nina Park (author): "Added lease_reclaimed_count metric and the session debug log; log is gated behind DEBUG to avoid noise in prod by default."
- Claire Zhou (reviewer): "Edge case: if a tool call is long-running and client reconnects after TTL, do we risk sending stale completion events? Suggest attaching confirmation id to completion ack as well."
- Nina Park: "Good catch — completion ack already included a call_id but not the confirmation id. Updated stream_adapter to include confirmation id on completion acks, and added tests."
- Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Can the fallback routing cause cold-start spikes on dedicated pools? Add a soft ramp or circuit-breaker."
- Nina Park: "Added a simple token-bucket guard and a configurable ramp parameter; documented in docs/operational/lease_and_heartbeat.md."

Merging and operational rollout: Merged via squash on 2026-02-21 after approvals. Feature flags: the heartbeat + confirmation flow is behind a runtime feature flag (runtime.features.stream_lease_v1) and default-on for new accounts. Ops runbook includes SLO dashboard widgets for lease churn rate and confirmation-id mismatch rate, and an alert if fallback_routing_rate > 1% sustained over 5m.

Potential follow-ups: tighter telemetry for cross-region resume latency, SDK ergonomics for exposing confirm ids to function-call handlers, and a long-term plan to expose lease diagnostics via the Console.
